label: Preservation capture: museum correspondence declaring Metaconceptual Art (2013)
note: The email thread of 2013-09-12 between Sun & Rain Works and the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art at the University of Oregon. The copy held is the one the museum retrieved from its own archive and supplied in July 2026, not a copy saved from the sending mailbox in 2013; its headers carry the university's internal Exchange routing and none of the sending provider's, so the message is institutionally retained rather than studio-held. This was private correspondence rather than something its author published, so the original is not published here. What is published is a redacted copy, and the SHA-256 of the unredacted original, so that original can later be shown to be unaltered without disclosing its contents.

redaction.policy: Third-party identity withheld pending consent, following the convention used throughout this collection. The name of the museum staff member who replied and both correspondents' mailbox addresses are replaced with '[name withheld]' and '[address withheld]'. The email domains are deliberately retained: uoregon.edu carries the fact of institutional receipt, which is the point of the record.
redaction.preserved: All headers bearing on the date are untouched: the recipient Exchange server's Date stamp, the Message-ID, and the four Yahoo message identifiers whose leading integers are server-written Unix timestamps. So is the full text of the studio principal's declaration and the substance of the museum's reply.
replacements: the replying staff member's name -> [name withheld]
the studio principal's then-current yahoo.com mailbox -> [address withheld]@yahoo.com

items.note: The message as received, with the identifiers above replaced. Stored with a .txt suffix so it is served as text rather than parsed. Byte counts differ from the original only by the length of the replacements.

items.role: unredacted original as supplied by the receiving institution, NOT published
items.note: Supplied by the museum in July 2026 from its own archive, in answer to an inquiry about its 2009 holdings. Held by the studio on separate media. This checksum is published so the held file can be shown to match what was described here, without the file itself being disclosed. It can be released, in whole or in part, if the third party consents.
items.provenance: Received from the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art, 2026-07-15, as an attachment to its reply. No Received headers and no sending-provider X-headers; four X-MS-Exchange-Organization headers, originating client address within UONET (128.223.0.0/16, University of Oregon).

dateEvidence.method: Five timestamps written by two unrelated mail systems, in monotonic order.
dateEvidence.note: The four Yahoo identifiers span sixteen minutes of one outbound thread and increase in order; the recipient's Exchange server stamped its reply two and a half minutes after the last of them. Those identifiers were generated by Yahoo and copied verbatim into the University of Oregon server's References and In-Reply-To headers, so the two systems corroborate each other. Local Pacific times are 16:19 to 16:35, consistent with the quoted 'Sent' line of 4:36 PM.

lostSources: The yahoo.com mailbox from which the thread was sent (address withheld, as in the redacted copy) - closed. The receiving institution's copy survives and is the file held.
YouTube videos cited in the letter as carrying the eight defining characteristics - no longer exist.
facebook.com/sunandrainworks - deleted; no Internet Archive capture exists.

negativeFinding.asked: 2026-07-11 - whether the museum's email archive reaches back to March 2009
negativeFinding.answered: 2026-07-15 - the museum holds no email from the studio's then-current address dated 2009
negativeFinding.scope: A search that returned nothing, not a demonstration that nothing was sent. Mail addressed to other staff, retention limits, and staff turnover are all unexcluded. The museum's holdings do reach 2013.
